title: Latency-driven region arbiter with multi-tier routing and staged-variant fallback
creator: Jin Park
description: Background: We need a robust region-selection service that combines latency percentiles (p50/p95) and network health signals into a single arbiter for routing decisions across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private tiers. Current routing uses simple percentile thresholds and static fallbacks; it does not account for short-lived network impairments nor does it gracefully stage fallback to cheaper/quantized model variants. Goal: build a latency-driven region arbiter that computes an aggregate 'region score' from p50/p95 telemetry and network health indicators (packet loss, 5xx rate, RTT variance), applies EWMA smoothing and hysteresis, and outputs weighted region priorities. Integrate with tier-routing policies so requests are first matched to customer tier (Dedicated -> Private -> Hosted) and then routed by region score. Add a staged-model-fallback engine: when a region degrades beyond thresholds, traffic is gradually shifted to a compatible variant (e.g., quantized/8-bit) in other healthy regions with canary probes before full cutover. Non-goals: changing model-serving internals or modifying model comparator evaluation; this ticket implements routing and policy orchestration only.
acceptance_criteria: Region score computed every 30s using blended p50/p95 with configurable weights and exposed via telemetry
EWMA smoothing and hysteresis prevent flip-flopping for transient spikes (<60s)
Automatic tier-aware routing honors customer tier preference and can force failover to next tier when region scores fall below policy
Staged fallback canary mechanism shifts up to 5% traffic to a fallback variant, evaluates quality and latency within 5 minutes before progressive ramp to 50%

Simulated load tests show <=5% increase in average token-cost after fallback; p95 tail across global requests improved by at least 10% compared to current static routing during injected network degradation
Dashboard tile in Console shows per-region score, contributing signals, and last decision timestamp
Rollback triggers exist: >2% error-rate increase or >20% downstream latency regression in canary => automatic rollback
Unit and integration tests cover score calculation, hysteresis window, and staged-fallback state machine
test_plan: Synthetic telemetry generator to emit controlled p50/p95 and packet loss; verify score moves as expected
Chaos test: inject latency/pktloss in primary region and observe canary, ramp behavior and rollback triggers
Backfill analysis on 30 days of historical telemetry to tune weights for p50 vs p95 for different model classes
E2E test with Dedicated, Hosted, Private tenants to validate tier routing and isolation of fallback variants
Load test with 200k requests/min with mixed prompt lengths to validate scaling and latency SLO preservation
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated rollout: off by default
Step 1: enable scoring read-only and expose metrics to Console (2d)
Step 2: enable observer mode — decisions computed but not enforced; compare against existing router (3d)
Step 3: enable active routing for 5% of traffic behind flag with canary fallback (3d)
Step 4: progressive ramp to 25% then 75% with monitoring checkpoints and manual approval
Step 5: full rollout and remove feature flag (only after two 48h monitoring windows are green)
notes: Design trade-offs: weight p95 higher for latency-sensitive models (chat) and p50 higher for bulk embeddings workloads; make weights per-model-group configurable
Decision: use EWMA with alpha=0.2 for short-term smoothing and add a 2-minute cooldown window for region demotion
Safety: always require health probe success in destination region before model-variant ramp beyond 10%
Privacy: only use aggregated telemetry; no per-token or per-user data is part of score
Operational: expose effective policy per-tenant in Console so support can explain routing decisions
